item.text: The Independent Commission Against Corruption surveyed NSW public sector organisations and staff to identify perceived corruption risks and existing prevention practices.
item.support:
In late 2001, the ICAC commenced a major research
project to develop a snapshot of corruption-related issues

item.text: It received completed surveys from 265 organisations and 357 staff across 20 organisations; the research explored potential opportunities for corruption rather than measuring existing corruption.
item.support:
The research does not quantify existing corruption.
Instead, it explores perceptions of potential opportunities
for corruption.

item.text: ICAC identified misuse of confidential information, misuse of public assets and corrupt tendering as the main perceived risks confronting organisations.
item.support:
An overview of the results suggests that the major risks
currently confronting organisations relate to misuse of
confidential information

item.text: ICAC made 29 recommendations covering risk management, conduct codes, gifts, information security, recruitment, procurement, audit, protected disclosures and internal investigations.
item.support:
ensure that internal reporting mechanisms are effective
and include protection for those that use them

item.quote:
However, public sector
organisations must remain vigilant in monitoring and
reviewing their risk management practices.

The ICAC encourages all organisations to adopt the
seven-step risk management process as a general approach
to identifying and treating risks.
